text:
Every Quinn Hughes shift now carries a second question: will he still be wearing a Wild sweater next fall? He is in the final year of his contract, there is no extension, and Sportsnet spent a column this week asking whether he stays. Hughes, for his part, told The Athletic's Michael Russo he's playing the best hockey of his career.

He is logging 28:11 a night, has 28 points in 21 games (6 goals, 22 assists) and is on a 10-game point streak. At five on five Minnesota takes 58.4% of the expected goals with him out there, 10.7 points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey ranked him first among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season.

One piece will fade: he is shooting 10.9% against a typical range near 6%, so the goals are running ahead of his usual pace. The assists are the real engine; Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his primary shot assists in the 99th percentile among defensemen.

Our range has him finishing between 84 and 110 points. Where he plays after this season is the story of Minnesota's winter.
